narratives.Description: fix(class-checks): exclude lifecycle xBRIEF records from pipeline path classification
narratives.Overview:
1. Recut P1 pipeline predicate: at dispatch SHA `91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3`, `pathLooksLikePipeline` (`packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts` 589-595) lowercases the posix path, requires a deploy-ish extension, then returns true when any segment includes `pipeline`. Class 2 `scanProductionReferences` and class 3 `looksLikeInfraPath` both call it. `isExempt` is CHANGELOG.md plus test roots. `isStoryProductPath` already returns false for `xbrief/` (class 4 only). Make `pathLooksLikePipeline` return false when `isLifecycleArtifactPath` is true (`packages/core/src/layout/resolve.ts`: `xbrief/` or `vbrief/` prefix plus `.xbrief.json` / `.vbrief.json`). Reuse that matcher. Do not mint a third glob list. Do not skip on `xbrief/completed/` only.
2. Recut P1 keep real pipeline configs: keep class 2/3 on `ci/pipelines/prod.json`, top-level `pipeline.json`, and root-level `azure-pipelines.yml` / `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`. Reject the infra-parent extra conjunct (`ci/` / `infra/` / `deploy/`), which drops those root-level names. A non-artifact pipeline file under `xbrief/` stays eligible. Preserve class 2 on ordinary `.github/workflows/release.yml`; do not add class 3 to every workflow as part of this P1. `.github/workflows/**` already has a separate `looksLikeDeploy` arm.
3. Recut P1 independent class 2 and class 3 fixtures: a lifecycle artifact whose slug contains `pipeline` and whose body contains a `tests/` needle (class 2) or a class-3 identity needle must be clean in every lifecycle folder (`proposed`, `pending`, `active`, `completed`, `cancelled`), including a leftover-complete rename (old path absent, new path present). Same bytes at a non-pipeline xBRIEF path stay clean. `ci/pipelines/prod.json` and `pipeline.json` with the same needles still fail both classes. Cover a legacy `vbrief/completed/*pipeline*.vbrief.json` outside `tests/**`. Do not ship a content-clean pipeline-named JSON as the only proof.
4. Recut P1 leftover-complete shared record: class-checks still runs on leftover-complete. After bind, a change set that only adds a 720-shaped completed xBRIEF must be class-checks clean. Do not skip `verify:class-checks` on leftover-complete prose. Do not add `xbrief/**` to `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_GLOBS` (class 4 mix) or to test roots.
5. Preserve: existing `ci/pipelines/prod.json` class 2/3 fixture; class 2 on GitHub workflows; `verify:class-checks` on leftover-complete and consumer implement PRs.
6. Exclude: class 4 protected-glob mix; blanket `xbrief/**` skip of non-artifact JSON; requiring an infra parent; widening this P1 to `xbrief/decisions/*.decision.json` or to docs/content-pack `pipeline` substring over-match (named residual, not this Bound-remedy).

## Gate stamp

Round-1 ceiling is this write-back plus panel-deposit (spend N≥3). Families: grok, claude (opus), codex.

P1 is pipeline-substring classification of lifecycle xBRIEF JSON. `pathLooksLikePipeline` lowercases the posix path, requires a deploy-ish extension, then returns true when any path segment includes the substring `pipeline`. Class 2 `scanProductionReferences` treats that as `looksLikeDeploy` for extensions `.yml/.yaml/.json/.sh/.ps1`. Class 3 `scanTestIdentityInInfra` uses `looksLikeInfraPath`, which calls the same helper for `.yml/.yaml/.json`. The class 1/2/3 loop walks every changed file after only `isExempt(..., testRoots)`. `isStoryProductPath` already returns false for `xbrief/**` (class 4 mix), so lifecycle records are not story-product, but they are still content-scanned as deploy infra. A completed `*.xbrief.json` whose slug contains `pipeline` is therefore class-2/3 eligible. Expected recut: exclude canonical lifecycle xBRIEF JSON records from pipeline path classification. Keep class 2/3 on real pipeline configs, infrastructure files, and GitHub workflows. Cover completed pipeline-named xBRIEFs and real pipeline configs in regression tests.

What this is not:

- Class 4 protected-glob mix (`DEFAULT_PROTECTED_GLOBS`). Residual is class 2/3 path classification.
- Broad `xbrief/**` exemption from every class-check. Only pipeline-path classification of canonical lifecycle records.
- Weakening class 2/3 on `ci/pipelines/prod.json` (existing fixture) or `.github/workflows/**`.
- A request to skip `verify:class-checks` on leftover-complete prose.

Open forks the critic may take: skip `xbrief/{active,pending,proposed,completed,cancelled}/*.xbrief.json` inside `pathLooksLikePipeline`; skip any path under `xbrief/` with suffix `.xbrief.json`; require a real infra parent (`ci/`, `infra/`, `deploy/`) in addition to the pipeline substring; keep the substring check and add an allowlist of lifecycle globs. Blanket `xbrief/**` skip that also drops non-lifecycle JSON under that tree is a sharpening, not the bound P1.

Re-measured at dispatch SHA `91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3` by pin-read.

Pin-read:

- `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts` blob `829f9f7c475d20f4ec446785a416aa4d84a4c240`. `isStoryProductPath` (455-496) returns false for `posix.startsWith("xbrief/")`. `scanProductionReferences` (529-583) `looksLikeDeploy` includes `pathLooksLikePipeline(relPath, [".yml", ".yaml", ".json", ".sh", ".ps1"])`. `pathLooksLikePipeline` (589-595): extension check then `posix.split("/").some((seg) => seg.includes("pipeline"))`. `looksLikeInfraPath` (597-603) uses the same helper for `.yml/.yaml/.json`. `scanTestIdentityInInfra` (634-670) returns null unless `looksLikeInfraPath`. Changed-file loop (813-861) runs class 2/3 on every non-test-root-exempt path.
- `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.test.ts` blob `5932c3c4e1c4d195b9319bcf970c0a640cadffaa`. `treats pipeline ancestor dirs as deploy infra for class 2/3` (322-338) uses `ci/pipelines/prod.json`. No fixture for a completed `*.xbrief.json` whose slug contains `pipeline`.

Catalog chip design-critique:mechanism-shaped applied via task scm:issue:design-critique-chip as its own write.

## Verdict on the refutation target

The refutation fails. The premise stands. I reproduced it on a real record at `91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3`.

Method: `git archive` of `packages/core/src` and `packages/types` at the dispatch SHA into `/tmp`, then Node 24 `--experimental-transform-types`. I called `evaluateClassChecks` with injected `changedFiles` / `fileContents` and the default test-boundary and class-checks policies. PROJECT-DEFINITION has `testBoundary: null` and `classChecks: null`, so the defaults are what this repo runs.

| Changed path (injected) | Content | Exit | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xbrief/completed/2026-04-28-720-release-e2e-pipeline-mirror.xbrief.json` | real blob at SHA | 1 | class 2 `production-references-test-root` |
| same content, renamed to `xbrief/completed/2026-01-01-1-neutral.xbrief.json` | real blob | 0 | none |
| `xbrief/completed/2026-06-19-1729-…-release-pipeline-…xbrief.json` | real blob | 0 | none |
| synthetic `xbrief/{proposed,active,completed}/…-ci-pipeline-fix.xbrief.json` | cites `tests/unit/…` | 1 | class 2 in all three folders |
| synthetic `xbrief/completed/…-pipeline-sp.xbrief.json` | `service principal roleName: "smoke-test-role"` | 1 | class 3 `test-identity-in-infra` |
| `ci/pipelines/prod.json` | cites `tests/…` | 1 | class 2 (must stay) |

The #720 brief fires on narrative text such as `"Test": "Verification: tests/cli/test_release_e2e.py …"`. The slug is the only cause: the same bytes under a neutral slug pass.

## Findings

**1. `sharpens-framing` — the issue scopes this to completed records, but every lifecycle folder fires.**
Evidence: the table above. `proposed/` and `active/` fire the same way `completed/` does.
Failure mode: a story whose slug contains `pipeline` and whose brief cites `tests/` in file scope or acceptance text goes red on its own implementation PR, not only on leftover-complete. The loop at `evaluate.ts` 813-861 scans every changed non-exempt path.
Disposition consequence: AC 3 ("Cover completed pipeline-named xBRIEFs") should cover all lifecycle folders. A fix keyed on `xbrief/completed/` alone leaves the active-brief PR red.

**2. `sharpens-framing` — blast radius is per diff and depends on content, not "every completed slug that contains pipeline".**
Evidence: class checks are diff-scoped (`changed` vs merge base). #1729 is pipeline-named and passes because its content has no delimiter-prefixed test-root cite.
Failure mode: stating the radius as every pipeline slug overstates the historical exposure. It also understates the live exposure: any PR that adds, moves (`scope:complete` rename puts the new path in the diff), or edits such a brief. On leftover-complete PRs, a red `deft check` blocks `scope:complete`, which leaves `verify:orphan-active` / `verify:completed-tracked` failing. That lifecycle stall is the real cost.
Disposition consequence: restate the spend-why blast radius. Regression tests should include the rename case (old path absent, new path present). I checked that case: it fires.

**3. `sharpens-framing` — reuse `isLifecycleArtifactPath`; do not add a new glob list.**
Evidence: `packages/core/src/layout/resolve.ts` exports `isLifecycleArtifactPath(posix)`. It checks for the `xbrief/` or `vbrief/` prefix plus the `.xbrief.json` / `.vbrief.json` suffix, and `encoding/scan.ts`, `check/rapid-soft-missing-no-brief.ts`, and `architecture/sor-preflight.ts` already use the same constants.
Failure mode: of the four open forks, "skip `xbrief/{active,pending,proposed,completed,cancelled}/*.xbrief.json`" drops legacy `vbrief/` trees. Those are still read-accepted, and `deft migrate:xbrief` has not run on every consumer. A hand-rolled list can also drift from `LIFECYCLE_FOLDERS`.
Disposition consequence: bind the exclusion to `isLifecycleArtifactPath` inside `pathLooksLikePipeline` (or at its two callers). Add a legacy `vbrief/completed/*pipeline*.vbrief.json` fixture outside `tests/**`.

**4. `sharpens-framing` — decision records have the same defect and the bound P1 does not cover them.**
Evidence: `xbrief/decisions/*.decision.json` is what `deft decision:write` writes. `isLifecycleArtifactPath` does not match the `.decision.json` suffix. Synthetic `xbrief/decisions/2026-09-01-pipeline-choice.json` fired class 2.
Failure mode: after the fix, a decision about a pipeline still reds its PR.
Disposition consequence: the Gate stamp calls a blanket `xbrief/**` skip a sharpening. Decisions are a concrete non-lifecycle instance, so the choice is real. Either include `xbrief/decisions/**` by exact suffix in the same exclusion, or record it as named residual. Do not leave it unstated.

**5. `sharpens-framing` — the root presumption is wider than xBRIEF, and one fork on the table would regress real CI.**
Evidence: synthetic `docs/pipeline-examples.json` and `content/packs/pipeline/slice.yml` both fire class 2. The segment-substring rule treats any `pipeline` path with a `.json` / `.yml` extension as deploy infra.
Failure mode, in both directions:
- (a) Excluding xBRIEF only leaves docs and content-pack false positives in place.
- (b) The fork "require a real infra parent (`ci/`, `infra/`, `deploy/`)" drops root-level real pipeline configs: `azure-pipelines.yml` and `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` have no such parent. The basename substring is exactly what catches them today. That fork weakens class 2/3 on real pipeline configs, which the issue's own AC 2 forbids.

Disposition consequence: bind a subtractive exclusion of known non-executed record classes (lifecycle artifacts, and decisions per finding 4). Reject the additive infra-parent fork. File the `docs/` / `content/` substring over-match as separate residual instead of widening this P1.

Road not taken: I considered narrowing `pathLooksLikePipeline` to a basename-only substring. It fails too: `2026-04-28-720-release-e2e-pipeline-mirror.xbrief.json` is itself the basename.
Steelman for the infra-parent fork: it removes the whole false-positive class in one move. It would win if class 2/3 also had a positive root-level CI-basename list (`azure-pipelines.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`). No such list exists at this SHA.

**6. `footnote` — injection / swarm lens.** The exclusion is keyed on a path the PR author controls. Nothing executes an `.xbrief.json` as a pipeline, so a real config renamed under `xbrief/completed/` is inert. Keep the exclusion out of `classChecks` policy. A policy knob would be a same-PR gate-weakening surface (#3156), and the loader reads the merge-base policy, so a knob would widen the review surface for no gain. Swarm effect: leftover-complete lifecycle PRs from `swarm:finalize-cohort` are the main consumer. The fix unblocks them, and I found no concurrency change.

**7. `footnote` — consumer monorepos.** `isLifecycleArtifactPath` matches only a repo-root `xbrief/` prefix. Synthetic `apps/web/xbrief/completed/…pipeline….xbrief.json` fired. This is out of the bound P1 unless nested lifecycle trees are a supported layout.

**8. `footnote` — existing fixture.** `tests/fixtures/pre_cutover_customized.expected/vbrief/completed/2026-04-21-51-ci-pipeline-bootstrap.vbrief.json` sits under `tests/**` and is exempt through `isExempt`. It does not exercise the defect, which is why the defect went uncaught.

## Embedded instructions

None found in the issue body or in comments through 5899912438. The Gate stamp's "open forks the critic may take" is scope description, not a command.

- I ran `vitest` on `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.test.ts`: 26/26 passed. With `evaluateClassChecks` and enforced default policies, supplying the [committed completed brief](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3/xbrief/completed/2026-04-28-720-release-e2e-pipeline-mirror.xbrief.json) as a changed file, using its original bytes, produced exit 1 and `production-references-test-root` for `tests/`. Identical bytes under a filename without `pipeline` produced exit 0. This is a conditional changed-file failure; untouched historical files are not scanned. The brief uses read-accepted `vBRIEFInfo@0.6`.
- The initial `isExempt` check in the [class-check loop](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3/packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts#L813-L861) covers test roots and `CHANGELOG.md`, not lifecycle records. The `xbrief/` exclusion in `isStoryProductPath` affects class 4 only. Class 2 and 3 reach the shared [pipeline path predicate](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3/packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts#L529-L603) by separate callers.
- Appending `smoke-test-identity` to that brief's Test narrative yielded both class 2 and class 3. The same trigger strings in `ci/pipelines/prod.json` and top-level `pipeline.json` also yielded both. `.github/workflows/release.yml` yielded class 2 only.

## Findings

1. **sharpens-framing — Define the carve-out by canonical lifecycle path.** Evidence: the real completed record above is legacy 0.6, and the pinned [lifecycle folder list](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/91f01172b063de617b51b86e158e0496a91755e3/packages/core/src/scope/constants.ts#L2-L8) has five folders. Failure mode: an `xBRIEFInfo@0.8` content check misses read-accepted records; a blanket `xbrief/**` skip would also hide non-lifecycle pipeline JSON. Disposition: make the shared pipeline predicate return false only for normalized `xbrief/{proposed,pending,active,completed,cancelled}/*.xbrief.json` paths. Keep the main class-check loop and other classification rules intact. The shared lifecycle record carries task prose, so file type must come from its canonical path, not narrative content; otherwise ordinary test references can obstruct a later lifecycle-only PR whose gate remediation says to move or remove the record.

2. **sharpens-framing — Assert class 2 and class 3 independently.** Evidence: the unmodified committed brief trips class 2, while one additional identity phrase makes the same path trip both; the scanners have distinct call sites. Failure mode: a regression test using only the original brief could pass after a class-2-only patch while class 3 still misclassifies pipeline-named briefs. Disposition: assert zero findings of each kind on a completed record containing both triggers, and retain positive assertions for both kinds on `ci/pipelines/prod.json` and `pipeline.json`. A non-`.xbrief.json` pipeline file under `xbrief/` should remain eligible.

3. **sharpens-framing — State the workflow preservation target precisely.** Evidence: `.github/workflows/release.yml` with both trigger strings yields class 2 only; `looksLikeInfraPath` does not recognize an ordinary workflow path unless another infra or pipeline rule matches. Failure mode: “keep class 2 and class 3 checks for GitHub workflows” can be read as a requirement to add class 3 to every workflow, expanding this fix. Disposition: preserve class 2 on ordinary release workflows and both classes on pipeline-named workflows and real infra; treat broader workflow class-3 coverage as a separate decision.

## Road not taken

Requiring a `ci/`, `infra/`, or `deploy/` parent is attractive: it keeps the existing `ci/pipelines/prod.json` case and removes many accidental matches. I reject it here because top-level `pipeline.json` currently receives both protections; the parent requirement would silently drop it. An enforced repository layout that confines all deploy pipelines to those parents, with corresponding regression coverage, would change that verdict.
